The other models ran as 2–4 processes sharing the L4 and the 12 CPU cores, so their times are inflated. Four image models were also scored alone by accident: they took 1.2–1.5x less time alone, with identical scores (rine-ldm 200 s, commfor 16.5 s, commfor-224 11.5 s, safe 6.5 s). Use the column for rough relative cost only.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
• Only the three face-based CLIP/PE detectors work well here.
  • gend-pe, gend and dfdet-clip reach AUC 0.92–0.96 and EER 0.13–0.17, and they are the only models above 0.8 balanced accuracy at the default threshold.
  • All three were trained on FaceForensics++ with aligned face crops, which matches this task.
  • Their AUC differences are within noise on this dataset. Paired bootstrap 95% CIs: gend-pe − gend +0.037 [−0.008, +0.087], gend-pe − dfdet-clip +0.040 [−0.008, +0.092], gend − dfdet-clip +0.003 [−0.028, +0.035].
  • dfdet-clip beats the next model, dfdc-selim, by +0.154 AUC [+0.058, +0.258].
  • The two DFDC winners are weak here. dfdc-selim (AUC 0.761) and dfdc-wm (0.699) are face-based too, but they were trained on DFDC fakes, not on this tool's output. Neither is clearly better than the image detectors: for example, dfdc-selim − rine is +0.016 AUC [−0.092, +0.181].
  • Most models are miscalibrated at the default threshold. They rank fakes above reals better than chance, but nearly all their scores fall below 0.5, so almost everything is called real:
  • rine and safe score every video below 0.5. They get 100% of reals and 0% of fakes right, giving exactly 0.500 balanced accuracy despite AUC 0.745 and 0.693. Their highest fake scores are 0.384 and 0.276.
  • univfd (AUC 0.719) catches 1.9% of fakes; commfor-224 catches 3.8% and commfor 13.2%.
  • dfdc-selim catches 18.9% of fakes and dfdc-wm 26.4%, while getting 92–94% of reals right.
  • These models need a threshold chosen on in-domain data before their binary decisions are usable. AUC and EER are the fairer comparison for them.
  • gend and gend-pe lean the other way. They catch 94–96% of fakes but get only 68% and 76% of reals right, so they will raise false alarms on real faces at 0.5. dfdet-clip is more balanced at 0.5: it gets 89% of reals and 76% of fakes right.
  • clipdet is the best calibrated image detector at 0.641 balanced accuracy. Its AUC (0.712) is in line with the other image detectors.
  • The image detectors are expected to be weak here.
  • univfd, rine, rine-ldm, commfor, commfor-224, safe and clipdet were trained to flag whole images from GANs and diffusion models (ProGAN, Latent/Stable Diffusion and similar).
  • In a face swap, the background, body and most of the frame are untouched real camera footage, and only the face region is generated and blended in. That region is a small part of a 1280x720 frame.
  • Several of these models score only a central crop without resizing, so they may not see the face at all.
  • Their AUCs of 0.56–0.75 show some weak signal. All of their 95% CIs reach down to between 0.45 and 0.62, and rine-ldm's includes 0.5. They should not be used as face-swap detectors based on this run.

docs.title: Follow-up 1: image detectors on face crops
docs.text:
The main run fed whole frames to the image detectors. As a follow-up, the same 8 frames per video were cropped around the largest face before scoring.

  • Option: --face-crop, added to scripts/eval_video_folder.py for this.
  • Crop: MTCNN, 1.3x the face box, at least 256 px a side, never resized, so each model's own preprocessing still applies.
  • Frames without a face: dropped. Every video kept at least one.
  • Results: results/sdfvd_facecrop.json, results/sdfvd_facecrop_scores.csv, results/sdfvd_facecrop.log.
  • Gain: the change in AUC from full frames to face crops on the same videos. Its 95% CI comes from 5,000 bootstrap resamples (reals and fakes drawn separately, seed 0), applied to both inputs.
Model AUC, full frame AUC, face crop [95% CI] Gain [95% CI] EER, face crop Bal. acc @0.5, face crop commfor 0.697 0.878 [0.810, 0.936] +0.181 [+0.077, +0.289] 0.226 0.679 commfor-224 0.642 0.848 [0.768, 0.915] +0.206 [+0.111, +0.302] 0.226 0.632 rine 0.745 0.844 [0.761, 0.916] +0.100 [+0.010, +0.194] 0.189 0.509 univfd 0.719 0.818 [0.729, 0.897] +0.099 [+0.012, +0.192] 0.189 0.547 safe 0.693 0.722 [0.622, 0.811] +0.028 [−0.055, +0.110] 0.358 0.500 rine-ldm 0.561 0.694 [0.585, 0.787] +0.133 [+0.019, +0.244] 0.396 0.585 clipdet 0.712 0.678 [0.571, 0.777] −0.033 [−0.134, +0.065] 0.377 0.632
  • Five of the seven models improve significantly on face crops; safe and clipdet don't change significantly. This supports the earlier explanation: on full frames, the center crop often missed the swapped face.
  • The best image detectors on crops (commfor, commfor-224, rine) are still below the face-based video detectors (gend-pe 0.956, gend 0.919, dfdet-clip 0.916).
  • The miscalibration remains. At 0.5, rine, univfd and safe still call almost every video real.
  • The rine row uses unrounded scores. The results files store per-video scores rounded to 6 decimals, and many of rine's scores round to 0 (36 of 106 full-frame scores, 20 of 106 face-crop scores). Recomputing its AUC from the stored scores therefore gives 0.719 instead of 0.745 for full frames. The AUCs in the JSON models entries were computed before rounding and are correct. The rine gain was computed from a rerun that kept full precision; it matched the stored scores after rounding.

docs.title: Follow-up 2: calibration
docs.text:
forensix/calibration.py and scripts/recalibrate.py (see the README's Calibration section) fit, per model:

  • a Platt scaling of the score;
  • a split-conformal threshold on real videos only, so the false-alarm rate is at most α;
  • conformal prediction sets.

Out-of-fold results. To estimate how calibration behaves on unseen videos, the scores in results/sdfvd_scores.csv were cross-validated:

  • 5 folds, seed 0, α = 5%.
  • Each real/fake pair (vN, vsN) is kept in the same fold, so a model is never calibrated on one half of a pair and tested on the other.
  • Results are in results/calibration_sdfvd.json.
  • The tables in calibrations/sdfvd/ are then fitted on all 106 videos.
Model AUC Bal. acc @0.5, raw Bal. acc, Platt ECE, raw ECE, Platt False alarms, conformal (α = 5%) Detection, conformal Single-label sets gend-pe 0.956 0.859 0.887 0.116 0.081 5.7% 67.9% 72.6% gend 0.919 0.811 0.821 0.125 0.049 5.7% 54.7% 67.9% dfdet-clip 0.916 0.821 0.849 0.126 0.091 5.7% 49.1% 59.4% dfdc-selim 0.761 0.566 0.698 0.342 0.071 3.8% 18.9% 30.2% rine 0.719* 0.500 0.641 0.488 0.122 7.5% 28.3% 17.9% univfd 0.719 0.509 0.660 0.442 0.062 3.8% 22.6% 22.6% clipdet 0.712 0.641 0.689 0.052 0.114 3.8% 11.3% 13.2% dfdc-wm 0.699 0.594 0.641 0.305 0.093 3.8% 15.1% 22.6% commfor 0.697 0.557 0.660 0.399 0.096 3.8% 24.5% 21.7% safe 0.693 0.500 0.632 0.451 0.033 3.8% 20.8% 18.9% commfor-224 0.642 0.509 0.632 0.470 0.077 3.8% 3.8% 14.1% rine-ldm 0.561 0.528 0.528 0.106 0.006 3.8% 3.8% 7.5%

* Computed from the rounded scores in the CSV (see Follow-up 1); 0.745 at full precision.

  • Calibration changes the threshold, not the ranking. AUC is unchanged by construction.
  • Platt scaling fixes the "everything is real" problem. Models whose balanced accuracy at 0.5 was about 0.50 reach 0.63–0.70. ECE drops for every model except clipdet (0.052 → 0.114), which was already the best calibrated.
  • The conformal threshold held its false-alarm target out of fold. Observed rates were 3.8–7.5% at α = 5%. With about 10 reals per fold, each rate has wide error.
  • It catches few fakes for the weak models. The cost of a guaranteed false-alarm rate is low detection: 49–68% for the three GenD models, and at most 28% for the others.
  • Prediction sets are often {real, fake}. That means "this score doesn't support a decision at 95% confidence". The single-label column shows how often a model commits.
  • The tables were fitted on SDFVD. They encode Remaker AI swaps on Pexels clips. Refit them on data like yours before using them; scripts/recalibrate.py check tests whether a table still fits new labelled data.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Small sample. With 53 real and 53 fake videos, the 95% CI on AUC is about ±0.03–0.05 for the top models and about ±0.1 for models near AUC 0.7 (see the table). Differences of a few AUC points are not meaningful, and the ranking from dfdc-selim down to commfor is not reliable. Accuracy at a threshold has binomial error of up to about ±0.13 per class (95%, n=53).
  • One face-swap tool. All fakes come from Remaker AI on short Pexels clips. These results say nothing about other face-swap tools, reenactment, lip-sync, fully generated videos, or heavily compressed (social-media) footage.
  • Face detector substitution. Upstream GenD uses the SCRFD face detector. ForensiX uses MTCNN for gend, gend-pe and dfdet-clip (see forensix/video/gend/__init__.py), so their face crops can differ slightly from upstream.
  • Image detectors on video. The main table uses whole frames. Face crops change the numbers substantially; see Follow-up 1.
  • Timing. Times other than univfd and rine were measured with other models sharing the GPU (see the Results notes).
  • Run history. The run was split across processes to use the whole GPU:
  • univfd and rine come from a sequential run of the command below.
  • The other ten models come from parallel runs of the same script with --models subsets and their own --out files, merged into results/sdfvd.json.
  • Then the command below was rerun; it skipped all 12 models and wrote the CSV.
  • Splitting doesn't change scores. rine was scored twice, and rine-ldm, commfor, commfor-224 and safe were scored both alone and in parallel; per-video scores were identical every time. results/sdfvd.log has the full history.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
# from the repo root, with ForensiX installed (pip install -e .) and a CUDA GPU
mkdir -p /content/sdfvd && cd /content/sdfvd
curl -L -o sdfvd.zip "https://data.mendeley.com/public-files/datasets/bcmkfgct2s/files/a9ef71a3-b625-4682-a21c-f0579e85cdd4/file_downloaded"
echo "734a101fdfd89d5b20ac69f510d6a7cf3b588a145c1993ba2488322ae50d95a5  sdfvd.zip" | sha256sum -c
unzip -q sdfvd.zip && cd -

export FORENSIX_CACHE=/path/to/forensix_cache   # optional; about 6 GB of weights
python scripts/eval_video_folder.py --device cuda \
  --real /content/sdfvd/SDFVD/videos_real --fake /content/sdfvd/SDFVD/videos_fake \
  --dataset SDFVD \
  --models univfd rine rine-ldm commfor commfor-224 safe clipdet gend gend-pe dfdet-clip dfdc-wm dfdc-selim \
  --out results/sdfvd.json --scores-out results/sdfvd_scores.csv

Follow-ups (same downloads):

# 1. image detectors on face crops
python scripts/eval_video_folder.py --device cuda --face-crop \
  --real /content/sdfvd/SDFVD/videos_real --fake /content/sdfvd/SDFVD/videos_fake --dataset SDFVD \
  --models univfd rine rine-ldm commfor commfor-224 safe clipdet \
  --out results/sdfvd_facecrop.json --scores-out results/sdfvd_facecrop_scores.csv
# 2. calibration: cross-validated report and one table per model, from the stored scores
python scripts/recalibrate.py fit --scores results/sdfvd_scores.csv --group-regex '(\d+)' \
  --alpha 0.05 --out-dir calibrations/sdfvd --report results/calibration_sdfvd.json

The script resumes: models already in --out are skipped. To use more of a large GPU, run several copies with disjoint --models lists and separate --out files, then merge their models and scores entries. The metrics are unchanged.

docs.title: Audio-visual detectors: LAV-DF
docs.text:
This report evaluates the three audio-visual detectors with released weights (syncnet, stablesyncnet, avad) on LAV-DF. It also calibrates them on one split and checks the calibration on another. avcons and avid aren't included, because they have no released weights: you train them on your own real videos.

Raw results: - results/lavdf/lavdf_test.json, results/lavdf/lavdf_dev.json (metrics); - results/lavdf/{test,dev}/*.jsonl.gz (per-clip and per-window scores, gzipped); - results/lavdf/lavdf_{test,dev}_scores.csv (one row per clip); - results/lavdf/calibration_lavdf_dev.json and calibrations/lavdf/ (calibrations).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The two lip-sync models detect LAV-DF fakes moderately well.
  • Clip AUC: stablesyncnet 0.785 [0.753, 0.819], syncnet 0.722 [0.688, 0.757].
  • They catch edits to the audio, the video and both at similar rates, which fits a sync check: any word edit breaks lip-sync.
  • Score a clip by its most suspicious window, not the mean.
  • LAV-DF edits are short (median 0.66 s in a 7 s clip), and the mean dilutes them.
  • This rule was chosen on the dev split and then tested on test. It raises test AUC to 0.853 for stablesyncnet (+0.068 [+0.043, +0.093], paired) and 0.833 for syncnet (+0.110 [+0.078, +0.143]).
  • With this rule, the two models' AUCs are within noise of each other (difference +0.017 [−0.013, +0.048]).
  • The windows roughly locate the edit. Windows that overlap a fake segment score above windows of real clips with AUC 0.83–0.85.
  • avad is near chance (0.563 [0.525, 0.601]).
  • Following upstream, it scores only the first 50 frame-steps (about 2.2 s) of the face track. Most LAV-DF edits come later, and it can't see them (AUC 0.50–0.55 on those).
  • Even on edits inside that window, it reaches only about 0.6, and about 0.5 on audio-only edits.
  • Calibration transferred from dev to test for stablesyncnet but not for syncnet.
  • stablesyncnet with the worst-window score: 2.5% false alarms at a 5% target, ECE 0.03.
  • syncnet flagged 10.7–12.0% of test reals, against the 5% target. Its real scores shift with clip length, and that length mix differs between splits.
  • scripts/recalibrate.py check flags exactly these two tables for recalibration.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
• Name: LAV-DF, "Localized Audio Visual DeepFake" (Cai et al., DICTA 2022).
  • Link: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ControlNet/LAV-DF
  • License: CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial research and education only. It's built from VoxCeleb2, whose terms also apply. Access is gated on Hugging Face.
  • Archive: LAV-DF.tar, 25,607,198,720 bytes, sha256 2abc0646cf1469f0bebec60a792fec8b6d670cd9e6133105139110c4316b20a4. Downloaded on 2026-10-26 to /content/lavdf, outside the repo.
  • Content: 136,304 VoxCeleb2 talking-head clips. Each fake replaces one or two words, with content-driven edits generated in the visual track, the audio track or both. Fake segments last 0.2–1.1 s (5th–95th percentile; median 0.66 s). Test clips last 4.4–16.8 s (median 7.1 s).
  • Subsets (sampled with scripts/eval_lavdf.py, seed 0, equal numbers per class):
Split Real Audio edited Video edited Both edited Used for test 300 300 300 300 all reported results dev 200 200 200 200 choosing the clip score; fitting calibrations

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Hardware: NVIDIA L4 (23 GB), 12 CPU cores, Google Colab Pro.
  • Date: 2026-10-26.
  • Code: ForensiX 124205e plus the uncommitted changes listed under "Code changes" below.
  • Runtime: 9 processes (3 per model) sharing the GPU, at about 7 s per clip per process, so about 1.3 clips/s in total. A single process takes about 4.5 s per clip.
  • Scores (higher = more likely fake):
Model Clip score Windows syncnet −LSE-C confidence per 25 fps frame (median-filtered confidence) stablesyncnet 1 − mean sync probability non-overlapping 0.64 s windows avad anomaly score (KL divergence) none reported
  • Skipped clips:
  • stablesyncnet refuses clips whose face is tracked in under 90% of frames. It skipped 87 of 1,200 test clips (7%: 23 real, 24 audio, 21 video, 19 both) and 64 of 800 dev clips.
  • Its numbers cover only the clips it scored. In deployment, a skipped clip gets no answer.
  • The other two models scored every clip.

docs.title: Results (test, 1,200 clips)
docs.text:
Model Clip AUC [95% CI] AP EER Audio edited Video edited Both edited Worst-window clip AUC Window AUC stablesyncnet 0.785 [0.753, 0.819] 0.899 0.285 0.807 [0.771, 0.842] 0.784 [0.744, 0.823] 0.766 [0.726, 0.804] 0.853 [0.828, 0.878] 0.834 syncnet 0.722 [0.688, 0.757] 0.872 0.343 0.751 [0.714, 0.788] 0.704 [0.663, 0.745] 0.711 [0.671, 0.751] 0.833 [0.810, 0.856] 0.847 avad 0.563 [0.525, 0.601] 0.772 0.463 0.518 [0.472, 0.563] 0.578 [0.533, 0.623] 0.593 [0.547, 0.641] – –
  • CIs: stratified bootstrap with 2,000 resamples (reals and fakes drawn separately), seed 0.
  • AP: 900 of the 1,200 clips are fakes, so a random detector scores AP 0.75. Compare APs with that baseline.
  • Per-modality columns: each kind of fake is compared against the same 300 reals.
  • Window AUC: windows that overlap a fake segment, against all windows of real clips. Windows from the same clip are correlated, so no CI is given.

Choosing the clip score. The clip score was chosen on dev before looking at the test result for that choice:

Model Dev: mean Dev: worst window Test: mean Test: worst window Test gain, paired [95% CI] syncnet 0.760 0.870 0.722 0.833 +0.110 [+0.078, +0.143] stablesyncnet 0.810 0.851 0.786 0.853 +0.068 [+0.043, +0.093]

The detectors' own fake_prob is still the mean, so parity with upstream is unchanged. The worst-window score is computed from the per-window details that both detectors already return.

avad and its 2.2 s limit. Its 50-step limit is upstream's own (detect.py test2, max_len=50), and ForensiX matches upstream on this (see the README's Verification table).

Test fakes n AUC vs reals edit starts in the first 2.16 s 351 0.592 … audio edited only 113 0.505 … video edited 122 0.627 … both edited 116 0.639 edits only after 2.16 s 549 0.545

docs.title: Calibration (fit on dev, evaluated on test)
docs.text:
Fitting. scripts/recalibrate.py fit fitted one table per score on the dev clips, with α = 5% (calibrations/lavdf/). - syncnet's scores and avad's anomaly scores aren't probabilities, so they use Platt scaling on the raw score. recalibrate.py detects this automatically when scores fall outside [0, 1]; this support was added for this evaluation. - The test split was used only for the evaluation below.

Score Test false alarms (target 5%) Test detection Bal. acc, Platt ECE, Platt Real coverage Fake coverage Single-label sets stablesyncnet worst window 2.5% 36.5% 0.723 0.030 97.5% 93.5% 45.0% stablesyncnet 7.2% 27.0% 0.677 0.048 92.8% 94.1% 36.8% syncnet worst window 10.7% 65.8% 0.656 0.050 89.3% 95.1% 62.6% syncnet 12.0% 32.6% 0.587 0.047 88.0% 97.1% 34.7% avad 4.0% 4.4% 0.500 0.001 96.0% 95.3% 9.7%

syncnet's threshold doesn't carry over to test. - The conformal guarantee holds only if new real clips are exchangeable with the calibration reals. For syncnet they aren't. - Its real-clip scores differ between dev and test (KS p = 0.015). The score depends on clip length (Spearman ρ = −0.36), and the test reals are slightly shorter (median 5.9 s vs 6.4 s). - recalibrate.py check on the test scores flags syncnet and syncnet-max-window for recalibration (exit status 3). The stablesyncnet and avad tables pass. - In deployment, calibrate syncnet on clips with the same length mix as the traffic, or run check on a labelled sample regularly.

Other points. - Platt probabilities are well calibrated on test (ECE 0.03–0.05), even where the conformal threshold isn't. - stablesyncnet's own 0.5 threshold gives 0.53 balanced accuracy on dev (it calls almost every clip real). Platt scaling raises that to 0.68 on test. - avad's calibration is "correct" but useless: its probabilities stay near 0.5 and it detects almost nothing.

docs.title: Code changes
docs.text:
• forensix/calibration.py: a score_type field ("probability" or "raw") for calibrating scores that aren't probabilities. Existing tables load as "probability" and behave as before. Added test: tests/test_calibration.py::test_raw_scores_are_calibrated_without_logit.
  • scripts/recalibrate.py: picks the score type per model automatically, or with --raw-scores. Raw-score models get no "raw" probability metrics in the CV report.
  • forensix/audiovisual/stablesyncnet: the detail window_start_s gives each window's start time. The window-selection rule moved into window_starts(), used by both scoring and the details, so scores are unchanged (tests/test_audiovisual.py passes).
  • scripts/eval_lavdf.py (new): sampling, resumable sharded scoring, the report and calibration checks.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• LAV-DF is one kind of fake. Edits are short word replacements in VoxCeleb2 interviews. These results say nothing about face swaps, full-clip lip-sync dubbing, or other generators.
  • License. LAV-DF is non-commercial. These numbers can be shared for research, but the data can't be used to build a commercial product.
  • Model training data. stablesyncnet was trained on VoxCeleb2, the source of LAV-DF's real clips, so it may have seen some of these speakers or videos. syncnet (BBC television) and avad (LRS2) weren't trained on it.
  • stablesyncnet's skips (7% of clips) aren't counted as errors in its AUC.
  • Sample size. 300 clips per class gives AUC CIs about ±0.035 wide. Per-modality differences within a model aren't significant.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
# accept the terms at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ControlNet/LAV-DF, then: hf auth login
hf download ControlNet/LAV-DF LAV-DF.tar --repo-type dataset --local-dir /content/lavdf
echo "2abc0646cf1469f0bebec60a792fec8b6d670cd9e6133105139110c4316b20a4  /content/lavdf/LAV-DF.tar" | sha256sum -c
mkdir -p /content/lavdf/extracted && tar -xf /content/lavdf/LAV-DF.tar -C /content/lavdf/extracted
D=/content/lavdf/extracted/LAV-DF
# score (run shards in parallel: --shard 0/3, 1/3, 2/3 per model)
python scripts/eval_lavdf.py score --data $D --split test --per-class 300 --models syncnet stablesyncnet avad --out-dir results/lavdf
python scripts/eval_lavdf.py score --data $D --split dev --per-class 200 --models syncnet stablesyncnet avad --out-dir results/lavdf
python scripts/eval_lavdf.py report --data $D --split dev --out-dir results/lavdf
# calibrate on dev, evaluate on test, check for drift
python scripts/recalibrate.py fit --scores results/lavdf/lavdf_dev_scores.csv --alpha 0.05 --source lavdf-dev \
    --out-dir calibrations/lavdf --report results/lavdf/calibration_lavdf_dev.json
python scripts/eval_lavdf.py report --data $D --split test --out-dir results/lavdf --calibration-dir calibrations/lavdf
python scripts/recalibrate.py check --calibration-dir calibrations/lavdf --scores results/lavdf/lavdf_test_scores.csv

docs.title: Identity-based detection: voice (ASVspoof 2019 LA)
docs.text:
This report covers identity-based (reference-based) detection on ASVspoof 2019 LA: - id-voice: enrolls a person from reference recordings, then checks whether new audio is their voice. - Fusion with a countermeasure (CM): id-voice is combined with aasist, an audio deepfake detector that checks how the audio was made. This setting is spoofing-aware speaker verification (SASV): accept only the real person, speaking for real.

Results: results/sasv_asvspoof2019_la.json. Face and video identity (id-face, id-motion) aren't covered yet; that needs DeepSpeak v2 (access requested, see the end).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
System (eval) SV-EER SPF-EER SASV-EER id-voice alone 0.76% 28.10% 21.27% organisers' baseline ASV (for reference) 2.46% 45.88% 34.49% aasist alone (CM) 50.30% 1.38% 24.43% id-voice + aasist, fused 1.60% 2.05% 1.92%

All three columns are EERs with genuine trials as positives: - SV-EER: against other speakers. - SPF-EER: against spoofs. - SASV-EER: against both.

  • id-voice tells people apart well. It separates the target speaker from other speakers at 0.76% EER, better than the organisers' baseline ASV (2.46%).
  • Voice clones fool it. At its equal-error threshold, id-voice accepts 66% of spoofed trials, which are TTS and voice conversion of the target speaker. With SpeechBrain's default threshold it accepts 81%. Speaker verification can't tell a good clone from the person.
  • aasist has the opposite weakness. It rejects spoofs but has no notion of identity, so it accepts every other real speaker (SV-EER 50%).
  • Fused, they cover each other: SASV-EER 1.92%. The fusion is a logistic regression on [voice cosine, CM logit] with 3 parameters. It was fitted on the dev split, whose attacks (A01–A06) are all different from eval's (A07–A19), so the eval result is on unseen attacks.

docs.title: Data and protocol
docs.text:
• Dataset: ASVspoof 2019 LA (ODC-By 1.0; LA.zip, sha256 208a7e4e…5e4ec), with the dataset's own ASV protocol files: ASVspoof2019.LA.asv.{dev,eval}.{female,male}.trn.txt for enrollment and …gi.trl.txt for trials.
  • Eval: 48 target speakers, each enrolled from 11 or 19 utterances (696 in total).
  • 5,370 genuine trials (target).
  • 33,327 trials by other speakers (nontarget).
  • 63,882 spoofs of the target speakers: 13 attacks, 4,914 each.
  • Dev: used only to fit the fusion and to measure thresholds.
  • Scoring:
  • Voice: cosine of each trial's embedding to the mean of the speaker's enrollment embeddings.
  • CM: aasist fake_prob from scripts/batch_infer.py, with ForensiX's default averaging over all 4.04 s windows.
  • All 96,081 files were scored, with no failures.
  • Run: NVIDIA L4, 2026-10-26. Embedding took about 30 min for 97k files; the CM took about 20 min (58 files/s).

docs.title: id-voice alone
docs.text:
Threshold (cosine) Genuine rejected Other speakers accepted Spoofs accepted SpeechBrain default, 0.25 0.02% 18.2% 81.3% equal-error threshold on dev, 0.417 0.63% 0.98% 66.2%

The default comes from SpeechBrain's SpeakerRecognition.verify_batch. It's too lenient for clips this short (2–5 s). The dev-measured threshold carries over to eval: about 1% errors in each direction. ForensiX keeps SpeechBrain's default; for short clips, pass your own threshold or calibrate it (see the README's Calibration section).

Spoofs accepted by attack, at the SASV equal-error threshold:

Attack A07 A08 A09 A10 A11 A12 A13 A14 A15 A16 A17 A18 A19 id-voice 43% 10% 0% 73% 71% 31% 5% 45% 63% 80% 0% 0% 0.1% fused 1.1% 0.04% 0% 19.0% 0.1% 4.7% 0% 0% 2.3% 2.8% 0% 0.04% 0%
  • The worst attacks for voice identity alone: A10, A11, A16 and A15 sound like the target speaker 63–80% of the time.
  • A10 is the fusion's weak spot: 19% of its spoofs are still accepted. The dataset's README lists it as a TTS system with a neural waveform model.
  • A17–A19 (voice conversion) don't reach the target's voice at all.

docs.title: Fusion
docs.text: The fitted weights are cosine 26.79, CM logit −0.727, bias −19.06. To accept a trial, a high voice similarity has to outweigh a CM that says "fake". At the SASV equal-error threshold, the fused system: - rejects 1.9% of genuine trials; - accepts 1.2% of other speakers; - accepts 2.3% of spoofs.

docs.title: CM parity check: aasist on the full 2019 LA eval
docs.text:
Scoring every eval file allowed a check of aasist against its published EER on the full 71,237-trial CM protocol:

Scoring of clips longer than 4.04 s CM EER upstream: first 4.04 s (shorter clips repeat-padded) 0.82% (published 0.83%) ForensiX default: mean over all 4.04 s windows 1.58%

The port matches upstream. ForensiX's documented averaging of long clips roughly doubles the in-domain EER, as it does for rawgat-st (README, Models). This report's CM and fusion results use the ForensiX default. Changing that default is a separate decision; see the README note.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Old attacks. ASVspoof 2019 LA's attacks date from 2019 or earlier. Current zero-shot voice cloning (e.g. ElevenLabs) is likely to sound more like the target, and to be harder for aasist, which was trained on this dataset's train split, attacks A01–A06. The fused result is in-domain for the CM.
  • Clean, matched audio. Enrollment and trials come from the same corpus (studio read speech). Expect higher error rates across channels, such as a phone call against an interview.
  • id-voice's embedding model was trained on VoxCeleb, which doesn't include these speakers.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
L=/content/asvspoof/LA; S=/content/sasv
for s in dev eval; do
  python scripts/eval_sasv.py embed --la $L --split $s --out $S/${s}_emb.npz
  python scripts/eval_sasv.py trial-list --la $L --split $s --out $S/${s}_files.txt
  python scripts/batch_infer.py --model aasist --inputs $S/${s}_files.txt --out $S/${s}_aasist.jsonl
done
python scripts/eval_sasv.py report --la $L --emb-dev $S/dev_emb.npz --emb-eval $S/eval_emb.npz \
    --cm aasist --cm-dev $S/dev_aasist.jsonl --cm-eval $S/eval_aasist.jsonl \
    --baseline-asv $L/ASVspoof2019_LA_asv_scores/ASVspoof2019.LA.asv.eval.gi.trl.scores.txt \
    --out results/sasv_asvspoof2019_la.json

docs.title: Next: face and video identity
docs.text: id-face and id-motion need real recordings of each person plus deepfakes made of that person. DeepSpeak v2 has both (consenting participants, face swaps and voice clones of them), and access has been requested on Hugging Face. With it, the plan is: - id-face against face swaps (expected to pass them: a swap is built to look like the person); - id-motion and avid against them (expected to catch them); - id-voice + CM against current commercial voice clones.

docs.title: Physics detectors: SDFVD and ASVspoof 2019 LA
docs.text: This report evaluates the physics-based detectors (phys-*). These are hand-built checks on physical constraints, with no trained classifier. They ran on SDFVD (video) and a subset of ASVspoof 2019 LA (audio). It also tests whether priors fitted on real data improve them. For the learned detectors, see benchmark.md.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• SDFVD: no physics detector beats chance.
  • phys-motion AUC 0.45 and phys-lighting 0.48.
  • phys-bloodflow never applies: every clip is under its 6 s minimum.
  • With the default priors, phys-lighting flags 100% of the real clips, so it isn't usable on this footage.
  • Face swaps keep the source video's head motion and scene lighting. The constraints these detectors check are mostly preserved by construction.
  • ASVspoof 2019 LA: near chance with the default priors.
  • phys-voice AUC 0.49 and phys-room 0.49.
  • With priors fitted on ASVspoof's own bona fide train/dev speech, phys-voice rises to AUC 0.62. It flags 26% of fakes, with 1.4% of reals violating any constraint.
  • Coverage is low: phys-voice measures 33% of trials (it needs 1.5 s of voiced speech) and phys-room measures 4% (it needs 6 s of audio).
  • The fitted priors are not shipped as the package default.
  • They fail the package's own tests: a real 10 s LibriVox recording scores 1.0.
  • The reason: some ranges learned from ~3 s ASVspoof clips don't transfer to longer speech (details below).
  • The default stays the provisional, hand-set priors. This is a decision for the maintainer; options are listed at the end.
  • Camera-consistency feature. One experimental feature, fixed in advance on a dev split of SDFVD, reached AUC 0.66 [0.50, 0.81] on the held-out test pairs. It is not added to the package (see below).

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Set Content Used for SDFVD 53 real Pexels clips + 53 Remaker AI face swaps of them, 2.1–5.8 s, 30 fps (CC BY 4.0) video detectors; all 106 clips ASVspoof 2019 LA train + dev, bona fide 5,128 clips, 40 speakers fitting priors (held-out speakers for false alarms) ASVspoof 2019 LA eval subset 1,000 bona fide + 77 per attack (13 attacks), seed 0 = 2,001 trials; the same subset as scripts/eval_asvspoof2019_la.py and the audio rows of the README audio evaluation

The ASVspoof eval clips were never used for fitting. The eval speakers are disjoint from the train and dev speakers.

docs.title: Video: SDFVD (default priors)
docs.text:
Detector Applies to AUC AP Reals with any violation Reals with score ≥ 0.5 Fakes with any violation phys-motion 47 + 47 0.446 0.479 42.6% 10.6% 31.9% phys-lighting 47 + 47 0.481 0.489 100% 70.2% 97.9% phys-bloodflow 0 – – – – – max over detectors 47 + 47 0.487 0.495
  • Six of the 53 pairs have a face tracked in under 80% of frames, so they are skipped.
  • phys-bloodflow skips every clip (it needs at least 6 s).

Per constraint (raw measurement as the score, oriented so that higher means more suspicious; independent of the priors):

Constraint n AUC phys-motion/rotation_hf_energy_ratio 47 + 47 0.620 phys-motion/p99_angular_acceleration_deg_s2 47 + 47 0.556 phys-motion/p99_angular_velocity_deg_s 47 + 47 0.514 phys-motion/rigid_deformation 47 + 47 0.422 phys-motion/jaw_lip_coupling 4 + 4 0.438 phys-lighting/face_scene_coupling 17 + 17 0.561 phys-lighting/light_direction_jitter_deg 47 + 47 0.510 phys-lighting/shading_residual 47 + 47 0.508

With 47 pairs, a single AUC has a 95% interval about ±0.11 wide. So only rotation_hf_energy_ratio is even borderline, and it was not tested on held-out data.

phys-lighting flags every real clip. SDFVD's real Pexels clips fall outside its provisional ranges; the cause wasn't investigated. Fitting priors needs real video with labelled speakers or groups, and SDFVD's 53 reals are also the evaluation set, so no video priors were fitted here.

docs.title: Audio: ASVspoof 2019 LA subset
docs.text:
Detector Priors Applies to (real + fake) AUC AP Reals with any violation Reals with score ≥ 0.5 Fakes with any violation phys-voice default (provisional) 294 + 369 0.488 0.553 5.4% 0.3% 3.0% phys-voice fitted on ASVspoof train/dev 294 + 369 0.624 0.664 1.4% 0.3% 26.0% phys-room either 26 + 50 0.492 0.699 15.4% 0% 12.0%

For comparison, the learned audio detectors reach 0.0–3.1% EER on the same subset (see the README).

Per-constraint AUCs on the trials where phys-voice applies:

Constraint AUC longest_pause_free_s 0.789 hnr_db 0.695 jitter_percent 0.610 vtl_out_of_range_cm 0.500 f0_jump_rate_per_s 0.460 vtl_variation (276 + 205) 0.446

longest_pause_free_s is not a duration artifact. On these trials fakes are slightly shorter than reals (duration AUC 0.42). Within duration bins the constraint still separates well:

Duration AUC 3–4 s 0.88 4–6 s 0.86 6–20 s 0.92

The 2019 LA attacks rarely insert pauses. Normalizing by clip length (longest_pause_free_s / duration) gives AUC 0.88. That number was found by looking at this eval set, so treat it as a hypothesis for a future held-out test, not a result. It may not transfer to other generators.

Fitting the priors. - Command: scripts/calibrate_physics.py fit, α = 0.01, at least 100 real clips per constraint. - Held-out speakers (phys-voice, n = 236 clips): reals with any violation fell from 5.1% to 4.2%, and reals with score ≥ 0.5 from 1.7% to 0.8%. - The fitted values (results/physics/learned_priors_asvspoof.json):

Constraint Provisional (start, full) Fitted start Real median jitter_percent 0.25, 0.1 0.92 2.06 hnr_db 35, 45 17.0 9.7 longest_pause_free_s 12, 25 4.22 2.4 f0_jump_rate_per_s 2, 6 2.70 0 vtl_variation 0.12, 0.3 0.20 0.04 digital_silence_fraction (phys-room, n = 106) 0.2, 0.8 0.0 0

Constraints with fewer than 100 real measurements kept their provisional values. That covers all video constraints and three of the four phys-room constraints.

docs.title: Why the fitted priors are not the package default
docs.text:
The fitted table was installed as forensix/physics/learned_priors.json and the physics test suite was run. Three tests failed, and the file was removed:

  1. longest_pause_free_s starts at 4.22 s.
  2. That is the 99.8th percentile of real ASVspoof clips, whose median length is 3.3 s (95th percentile 5.3 s). Clips that short can't contain a long pause-free stretch, so the fitted range reflects clip length rather than speech.
  3. The test suite's real 10 s LibriVox recording has an 8.24 s pause-free stretch. It scores 1.0 (certain fake).
  4. digital_silence_fraction starts at 0.
  5. None of the 106 real ASVspoof clips long enough to measure had any digital silence, so any digital silence at all becomes a violation.
  6. This was fitted on only 106 clips.

The gate did its job: priors fitted on one corpus encode that corpus's recording conditions. The package therefore keeps the provisional priors. The fitted table stays in results/ for anyone scoring ASVspoof-like audio:

det = forensix.load("phys-voice")
det.load_priors("results/physics/learned_priors_asvspoof.json")

docs.title: Experiment: camera consistency on SDFVD
docs.text:
Idea. A face swap pastes a generated face into a real frame. The face region and its surroundings should then carry different sensor noise.

Protocol. - Fix a dev/test split of the 53 pairs before computing anything: seed 0, 27 dev pairs and 26 test pairs (split.json). - Explore features on dev only. - Choose one feature and its direction. - Evaluate it once on test.

Features explored on dev. All compare the inner face skin with a ring around the face, using the existing face tracker and skin mask. AUCs below use "higher = fake".

Feature Dev AUC (26 pairs) median noise ratio 0.50 median sharpness ratio 0.54 luminance flicker ratio 0.49 temporal noise ratio 0.47 noise_ratio_spread (std over frames of the log noise ratio) 0.34, i.e. 0.66 with lower = fake temporal noise ratio spread 0.33

Chosen before test. noise_ratio_spread, with lower = fake. In a swap, the face's noise tracks the surroundings less from frame to frame.

Test result (24 pairs; 2 pairs have too few tracked frames):

  • AUC 0.660, 95% CI [0.498, 0.812] from a stratified bootstrap, or [0.556, 0.771] when resampling pairs.
  • The fake has lower spread than its own real source in 71% of pairs. Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.0065 (two-sided).

Why it isn't in the package. - The effect is real on this held-out data, but small. - The physical story is weak. A swapped and re-encoded face could plausibly show more variation as easily as less. - Re-encoding by the swap service is a confound that could produce the same effect without any compositing. - One dataset and one generator are not enough evidence for a shipped detector.

Code and per-clip features are in results/physics/camera_experiment/.

docs.title: Fixes made during this evaluation
docs.text:
• forensix/physics/room.py.
  • Bug: when an analysis chunk reached the file's last samples, the speech mask was shorter than the chunk, and phys-room raised IndexError. It hit 7 of the ASVspoof clips.
  • Fix: pad the mask (one line).
  • Test: added a regression test, test_room_detector_chunk_at_end_of_file.
  • Not fixed: phys-voice raised "attempt to get argmax of an empty sequence" on 1 of the 5,128 fitting clips. That clip is excluded from the fit; the eval set was unaffected.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• SDFVD is small (47 usable pairs) and has a single generator. ASVspoof 2019 LA's attacks are older systems. Neither represents current deepfakes.
  • Every physics result here is close to chance, apart from phys-voice with in-domain priors. Use the physics detectors as interpretable side evidence, not as a primary detector.
  • No priors were fitted for video, because no separate labelled real video was available.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
These commands use the files in this repo. The data downloads are described in benchmark.md; ASVspoof 2019 LA is LA.zip from the Edinburgh DataShare (sha256 208a7e4e…5e4ec).

export FORENSIX_CACHE=/content/drive/MyDrive/forensix_cache
# SDFVD
for lab in real fake; do
  python scripts/calibrate_physics.py measure --media /content/sdfvd/SDFVD/videos_$lab --kind video \
      --label $lab --source sdfvd --out results/physics/sdfvd_$lab.jsonl
done
python scripts/calibrate_physics.py eval --measurements results/physics/sdfvd_{real,fake}.jsonl \
    --out results/physics/sdfvd_eval_provisional.json
# ASVspoof 2019 LA: symlink layout (fit = train+dev bona fide by speaker, eval = the README subset)
python results/physics/asvspoof/make_layout.py /content/asvspoof/LA /content/asvspoof/layout . --shards 6
for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5; do   # one process per shard; can run in parallel
  python scripts/calibrate_physics.py measure --media /content/asvspoof/layout/fit_$i --kind audio --label real \
      --source asvspoof2019-la-train-dev --out results/physics/asvspoof/fit_$i.jsonl
  python scripts/calibrate_physics.py measure --media /content/asvspoof/layout/eval_$i --kind audio \
      --labels-csv /content/asvspoof/layout/eval_labels.csv --source asvspoof2019-la-eval \
      --out results/physics/asvspoof/eval_$i.jsonl
done
python scripts/calibrate_physics.py fit --measurements results/physics/asvspoof/fit_*.jsonl --alpha 0.01 \
    --out results/physics/learned_priors_asvspoof.json
python scripts/calibrate_physics.py eval --measurements results/physics/asvspoof/eval_*.jsonl \
    --out results/physics/asvspoof_eval_provisional.json
python scripts/calibrate_physics.py eval --measurements results/physics/asvspoof/eval_*.jsonl \
    --priors results/physics/learned_priors_asvspoof.json --out results/physics/asvspoof_eval_learned.json
